summary: Sawtooth p95/p99 latency spikes on dedicated pool correlated with GPU thermal throttling
description:
Issue summary: Customer (Novus Health) reports recurring sawtooth pattern of p95 and p99 latency in their dedicated pool over the past 48 hours. Spikes occur every ~12-18 minutes and last 30-90s. Problem intermittently affects batch and streaming routes.

Impact: Production inference latency degradation for dedicated tenancy; elevated error budget risk and degraded customer experience for real-time clinical assistant. Customer reports trickle of failed requests during spikes (429/504) and increased tail latency.

Timeline: 2026-03-09 10:45 UTC first alert from customer on Slack; 2026-03-09 11:02 UTC automated p99 alert; 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC escalated to P1 after SLA window; 2026-03-10 09:10 UTC on-call started investigation.

Observed behaviours: Regular sawtooth latency with gradual ramp then abrupt recovery; GPU utilization dips (compute % falls) during spikes while kernel queue depth increases; telemetry shows simultaneous climb in GPU die temperature and GPU power reduction events on several hosts.

Why this looks unique: Unlike classic noisy-neighbor CPU saturation or burst-eviction patterns, the telemetry shows hardware-level thermal/power events driving transient performance regressions across tenants colocated in same rack. This matches thermal throttling on NVIDIA hosts rather than simple scheduler preemption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Novus Health dedicated pool config: model pin redwood-open-instruct-v2-dedicated, batch size = auto, concurrency cap = 16.
2) Run a mixed workload with 70% short streaming requests and 30% medium generation requests sustained for 30 minutes.
3) Observe p95/p99 latency in metrics/dashboard; watch GPU temperature and power telemetry for hosts serving the tenant.
4) Correlate with node-level logs for NVML power/cooling events and with rack PDUs for power capping events.
logs: Selected log excerpts and dashboards: dashboard/svc/dedicated/pools/novus-health/latency?from=2026-03-09T09:00Z, nvml-exporter/hosts/host-az1-rack12.log (see repeated 'Power cap event' and 'Thermal slowdown' entries), kubelet logs showing container reschedules for host-az1-rack12-ht1. Sample request IDs: rq_20260309_11a, rq_20260309_11b. Full packet captures and host NVML dumps uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-support/sup-41258/ (internal access only).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy tenant causing GPU memory pressure or scheduler evictions. Rejected after checking eviction and oom logs (no evictions recorded during windows).
Telemetry shows host-level power/thermal signals coincident with latency ramps. Several GPUs reported die temps crossing 85C and GPU clocks dropping by 300-400MHz during events.

Rack PDUs show brief power draw spikes followed by automatic rack-level power capping in the affected rack, likely triggered by co-located non-Redwood workloads on bare-metal tenants (partner experiments).

Autoscaler behavior: scaled up additional instances after spike begins, but new pods land on same rack because node affinity for dedicated pool is constrained; autoscaler couldn't place on cooler racks due to reserved capacity limits.
SRE runbook checked: thermal events fallback recommends evacuation and remap; we temporarily drained two nodes and rebalanced tenant across two cooler racks which reduced spike frequency.
comments: Avery Collins (Support) 2026-03-10T09:15Z: Customer observed repeating latency spikes; attached their client-side timing traces.
Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-10T09:42Z: Confirmed NVML thermal throttling entries on host-az1-rack12-ht1 and ht2. Scheduling immediate drain of ht1/ht2 and remap tenant to rack14.
Elena Park (Infra) 2026-03-10T10:05Z: Noted concurrent maintenance jobs started by partner tenant on rack12 at 09:50Z. Opened INT-9021 to track partner usage and PDU config.
Novus Health (Customer) 2026-03-10T10:40Z: After remap, tail looks better but still seeing two short spikes in the last hour; requested permanent mitigation and explanation for root cause.

Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-11T15:30Z: Scheduling kernel and driver upgrade on affected hosts, and changing autoscaler placement policy to prefer racks with average GPU temp < 65C for dedicated pools.
conclusion: Root cause appears to be rack-level power/thermal events causing GPU clock throttling on multiple hosts that serve the dedicated customer. The effect produced sawtooth tail latency spikes rather than sustained saturation. Contributing factors: constrained placement due to reserved capacity and absence of temperature-aware placement prior to this incident.
resolution: Mitigation applied: 1) Evacuated two hot nodes and rebalanced customer to cooler racks (completed 2026-03-10 11:20Z). 2) Worked with infra to disable non-critical partner jobs on rack12 and placed rack12 under maintenance. 3) Rolled out temporary scheduler rule: prefer nodes with GPU temp < 65C for dedicated pools (canary on 10% of clusters). 4) Plan: firmware/driver update and PDU config changes scheduled (INT-9021) and permanent change to autoscaler placement logic to consider historical rack temperature.
postmortem_action_items: 1) INT-9021: Work with partners to move heavy PDU draws off dedicated racks. Owner: Elena Park. ETA 2026-03-18.
2) PR-5601: Add GPU temperature metrics to placement scoring and implement placement penalization for racks exceeding thresholds. Owner: Runtime team. ETA 2026-03-24.
3) Ops task: schedule firmware/drivers update and run soak tests on affected hosts. Owner: Hardware team. ETA 2026-03-20.
4) Customer communication: send detailed incident summary and recommended tenant configuration changes (lowered concurrency cap and adjust burst windows). Owner: CS. ETA 2026-03-12.
customer_impact_summary: Novus Health experienced intermittent high tail latency (p95/p99) in prod for ~48 hours; functional correctness unaffected but experienced user-facing slowdowns and a small number of failed requests during spikes. No data loss.
notes_for_follow_up: Monitor p99 and host GPU temp for 72 hours post-drain; if spikes recur, escalate to emergency hardware replacement for hosts showing repeated throttles.
